charter:
# Charter — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

S12 delivers the web app over the conveyor's served actions: 22 declared screens, one action client, SSE subscriptions and a Playwright suite that runs the real binary against a seeded database. The project row is closed; this charter is the retrospective record the v4 close gate requires, and it states the gate's measured status rather than claiming it.

The project's authority is the S12 slice plan (`docs/plans/slices/S12-ui-buildout.md`) and its gate: every spec asserts empty state, error state and happy path — a spec that only asserts the happy path fails review — and the coverage table has no orphan. The coverage half is met (the parity contract is signed and its native map present); the state half is not: three specs assert only the happy path, eight miss one state, and the eval-run screen has no dedicated spec. A test-only unit carries the repair, and this project's closure review is authored only after it lands.

The app owns no table, action or event; every write is an action invocation and every read is a declared projection. The review is the Architecture Board's under its published standing delegation; the tranche decision is the programme owner's. This charter claims neither.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, Phase A)

body.assignment: Deliver the web app for the declared screen set: every screen a route over the served actions, its states honest, and its suite on the real binary. The assignment is retrospective: the app shipped on its slice lanes and this statement records the architecture that shipped, at the 2026-11-28 snapshot.
body.scope: The shell, the 22 declared screens and their screen modules, the action client, the SSE subscriptions and the Playwright suite; and the seven A–D artefacts. Out of scope: the workflow editor (S13), the V2 destinations (T18), the cutover (S14) and the read models themselves (their declaring slices).
body.responsibilities: The UI owner builds the screens and the suite; each declaring slice owns the read model and action a screen renders; the accessibility reviewer runs the one pass after the last screen; the cutover owner reuses the same suite; the programme owner decides the tranche. No role signs its own gate.
body.acceptance_criteria: The acceptance is A1–A5 of the acceptance document, plus the closure review's outcome-vs-acceptance table. A1, A3, A4 and A5 are delivered; A2 is the gate and is carried by #965. The statement claims no tranche authority.
body.constraints: No client database, no runtime API mocks, no fixture in a production screen, no second rendering stack, and no self-approved screen that no slice declared. The dev cookie is dev-only; the deployed run uses the OIDC helper.
body.retrospective: This SoAW is authored at the 2026-11-28 retrospective snapshot against a closed project row. It describes what the delivered app is, names the measured gate gap and the unit that carries it, and records that the tranche authorisation is the review's act.

documents.title: User Stories — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# User stories

## Personas

The tenant user works the board, the cockpit and the authoring screens; the approver decides in the cockpit and sees who decided and through which channel; the eval pilot signs off on the eval screens; the operations user reads the admin and audit screens; the cutover owner runs the same suite against the deployed app.
## Stories

As a tenant user, I want a board that pages rather than hides its tail, so that a large programme stays workable. As an approver, I want each decision to show its decider kind and channel, so that an agent's decision is distinguishable from a person's. As an eval pilot, I want the input and grading reviews as full screens over one approval primitive, so that the number is trusted. As an operations user, I want the registry, its schema and the audit trail on one admin screen, so that the platform is inspectable.
## Scenarios

The board's keyboard and pointer moves survive a reload (`board.spec.ts`). The cockpit renders decided_by_kind and via.channel (`cockpit.spec.ts`). The eval sign-off screen shows every input and the pilot's grades (`eval-signoff.spec.ts`). The eval report derives its numbers from the run's result rows (`eval-report.spec.ts`). A search with nothing typed explains itself rather than sending an empty query (`search.spec.ts`).
## Verify

Each scenario names its spec in `apps/web/e2e/`. The happy path is evidenced today; the empty and error halves are the ones #965 completes for board, prompt-audit and eval-audit, and extends across the six specs missing an empty state and the two missing a rendered refusal.

documents.title: Acceptance Criteria — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Acceptance criteria

## Scenarios

A1: the 22 declared screens exist as routes with their screen modules and spec files (21 distinct files; screen 16 shares `evals.spec.ts`). A2: every spec asserts empty, error and happy. A3: the coverage table has no orphan. A4: writes go through the action invocation path. A5: the suite runs on the real binary against a seeded database.
## Verify commands

A1: `ls apps/web/e2e/*.spec.ts` and the plan's §5 table. A2: the spec audit — `apps/web/e2e/board.spec.ts`, `prompt-audit.spec.ts` and `eval-audit.spec.ts` are happy-path-only; six specs miss an empty state; two miss a rendered refusal. A3: `python3 scripts/check-parity.py --require-native`. A4: `apps/web/src/api.rs` and the specs' request assertions. A5: `apps/web/playwright.config.ts`.
## Results

A1, A3, A4 and A5 pass at the baseline: 21 screen specs exist, the parity contract is signed and its native map present (1300 rows; used 218, rare 295, unused 543, dropped 244), the action client is the only write path, and the harness runs the real binary. A2 is partial: 10 specs carry all three states, 3 are happy-path-only and 8 miss one state; screen 16 has no dedicated spec.
## Status

Delivered: A1, A3, A4, A5. Open: A2, carried by #965 (test-only, one PR). The project's gate is therefore not met at this snapshot, and this pack does not close the project; the closure review is authored once #965 lands.

documents.title: Definition of Ready — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Definition of ready

## Independent

A UI unit lands in `apps/web` and its spec; it needs no other unit's files. The real orderings are typed: the read model comes from the declaring slice and the cutover is S14's, neither of which this project's units edit.
## Negotiable

The outcome is the plan's screen table and gate; the markup, component split and exact assertions are settled at delivery, not in this brief.
## Valuable

A screen that shows its empty, error and happy state is what makes the UI's decisions auditable (`B1`), and the signed coverage check is what makes the delivery predictable (`B6`).
## Estimable

The baseline is `main@ea03b188a`, the files are named (the screen modules, the 21 specs, the parity check) and every acceptance command is a path or a check.
## Small

One unit is one issue, one branch and one PR; the remaining gate work is one test-only unit (#965) that edits spec files only.
## Testable

Every scenario names its spec; a screen with no empty or error state is a product finding raised on the unit, not worked around in the test.
## Dependencies

S12 declares `needs` on S01, S02, S04, S05–S11, S17 and S18; every one is built. The gate's remaining work depends on no other unit, and the closure waits on #965.

documents.title: Definition of Done — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Definition of done

## Acceptance criteria

One row per scenario A1–A5, each keyed by its command or spec. A unit is done only when every row has a result at the merge head; a suite green on a different revision is not the evidence.
## Evidence at completion

The command, its result and the merge SHA per row. A2's result is the spec audit's table; it is recorded as partial until #965 lands, and the closure review is written only after that.
## Repo gate

The repository's preflight is the compile and lint verdict; the PR's public CI is the final gate. The Playwright suite runs on the real binary against a seeded database, and no test is skipped to make the gate green.
## Merge and closure

One PR closes the unit's issue; the branch is deleted after the merge. The project closes only when its receipt is green at a pinned snapshot, which requires the closure review and the declared closure outputs that this pack deliberately does not author while the gate is partial.

documents.title: Architecture Analysis — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Architecture and analysis pack

## Current state

The app exists as 46 screen modules under `apps/web/src/screens`, served by the conveyor binary as wasm; 51 Playwright specs exist, 21 of them for the plan's screen rows. The action client in `apps/web/src/api.rs` resolves the served registry and posts invocations; SSE channels update the views. The parity contract is signed and its native map present, and the suite runs the real binary.
## Options considered

The alternative to a Leptos app over the action registry was a server-rendered admin, refused because the same actions must be callable from the web, the agent front end and MCP, and a second rendering stack would fork the write path. A mocked-API test harness was refused because a green run would then mean nothing; the real binary with a seeded database is the standard.
## Risks

The measured risk is a screen that loses a state and still passes its suite: three specs assert only the happy path and eight miss one state. The check is the spec audit and the unit #965; the risk is not waived. The other risks are a screen reading the database directly, closed by the action client being the only write path, and a fixture-backed production screen, refused by the harness and the parity check.
## Dependency map

S12 needs S01 (the shell and actions), S02 (auth), S04 (the action contract), S05–S11 (the read models and screens it renders), S17 and S18 (the benchmark and improvement views). The cutover is S14's, which reuses the same suite. No edge is open construction.

documents.title: Architecture Design — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Architecture design

## Context and boundary

S12 owns the web app: the shell, the screen modules and the Playwright suite. It owns no table, action or event; every write is an action invocation and every read is a declared projection. The workflow editor is S13's, not a twelfth row, and the V2 destinations are T18's; this design covers the 22 declared S12 rows.
## Aggregates, tables and actions

S12 adds no aggregate, table, action or event — a deliberate empty set recorded in the plan's decisions. The app consumes the registry: boards, cards, approvals, requirements, processes, evals, benchmarks and inference views are served by the slices that own them. The only state the app holds is view state, and the SSE subscription is a reader of the same projections.
## Decisions

One app, one tenant population, cutover by host. No screen calls the database. No screen renders a fixture in production. The copilot screen is declared by S10 and recorded as a CONTRACT-CHANGE REQUEST rather than self-approved. The suite runs the real binary; the dev cookie is dev-only and the deployed run uses the OIDC helper.
## Acceptance

A1–A5 of the acceptance document. A1, A3, A4 and A5 are delivered; A2 is the gate and is carried by #965, whose result the closure review will read.
## Architecture artefacts

The seven A–D artefacts: the stakeholder map, the driver and requirements catalogs, the solution concept, the capability map, the data catalog and the technology standards catalog. The data catalog is the record of what the app renders; the requirements catalog carries the gate and its measured gap.

documents.title: Inception Analysis — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Inception analysis

## Current state

At inception the app was a shell with a few screens and no coverage rule; the plan's screen table and the parity contract came later. The build delivered 22 declared rows, the action client, the SSE channels and the Playwright suite on the real binary. The plan's own amendment of 2026-11-09 records the process view and the process map as late additions.
## Reuse sources

The served action registry, the read models of S05–S20, the approval primitive, the parity contract and the OIDC helper. Reuse is the reason the app owns no store: a second read path would fork what the slices serve.
## Build vs reuse

Build the shell, the screen modules and the suite; reuse every read model and every write action. The accessibility pass is one review after the last screen, not a per-screen component library. The V2 destinations are T18's build, not S12's.
## Risks

The inception analysis named the risk of rebuilding S05–S11's components inside S12 and the risk of a mocked suite. Delivery honoured the first by one component per first-needing screen; the second by the real-binary harness. The remaining risk is the measured spec-state gap, carried by #965.

documents.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S12 UI Build-out (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Statement of Architecture Work

## Assignment

Deliver the web app for the declared screen set: every screen a route over the served actions, its states honest, and its suite on the real binary. The assignment is retrospective: the app shipped on its slice lanes and this statement records the architecture that shipped, at the 2026-11-28 snapshot.
## Scope

The shell, the 22 declared screens and their screen modules, the action client, the SSE subscriptions and the Playwright suite; and the seven A–D artefacts. Out of scope: the workflow editor (S13), the V2 destinations (T18), the cutover (S14) and the read models themselves (their declaring slices).
## Responsibilities

The UI owner builds the screens and the suite; each declaring slice owns the read model and action a screen renders; the accessibility reviewer runs the one pass after the last screen; the cutover owner reuses the same suite; the programme owner decides the tranche. No role signs its own gate.
## Acceptance criteria

The acceptance is A1–A5 of the acceptance document, plus the closure review's outcome-vs-acceptance table. A1, A3, A4 and A5 are delivered; A2 is the gate and is carried by #965. The statement claims no tranche authority.
## Contract

The delivery contract carries the commitments, the compliance method and the approval. This statement is its architecture half; the two are published together so the close gate reads one consistent record, and the closure review is authored once the gate is met.

risk.title: A screen loses a state and still passes its suite
risk.body: A spec that asserts only the happy path cannot fail when the empty or error state disappears. The audit measured three such specs and eight missing one state. #965 adds the assertions; the risk is not waived, and the project's gate stays unclaimed until it lands.
risk.response: close the gap with a test-only unit and re-run the audit

risk.title: A screen becomes a second store
risk.body: A screen that reads the database or caches a model it does not own would fork the read path and drift from the slice that serves it. The action client is the only write path; the design records the rule and the specs assert the requests.
risk.response: no client database; writes through the action invocation path only

risk.title: A mocked suite green-lights a broken screen
risk.body: Runtime request mocking would let the suite pass while the real API disagrees. The harness runs the real binary against a seeded database, and the deployed run uses the OIDC helper rather than the dev cookie.
risk.response: real binary, seeded database, no runtime mocks

issue.title: The gate is not met: three happy-path-only specs
issue.body: board, prompt-audit and eval-audit assert only a happy path. The project's gate sentence says a spec that only asserts the happy path fails review, so the closure review cannot be written as a pass until #965 lands.

issue.title: Eight specs miss one state and screen 16 has no dedicated spec
issue.body: Six specs have no empty-state assertion and two render no refusal; the eval-run screen is covered only inside evals.spec.ts. #965's parts P2 and P3 close them.

issue.title: The row was closed with no published closure review and no declared outputs

project_brief_output:
# Project brief

## Outcome

One web app over the conveyor's served actions: 22 declared screens with honest states, a single action client and a suite that runs the real binary. The outcome is true of the shipped app; the gate's state half is the measured gap a test-only unit closes.
## Boundary

In scope: the shell, the 22 screens, the action client, the SSE subscriptions and the suite. Out of scope: the workflow editor (S13), the V2 destinations (T18), the cutover (S14) and the read models (their declaring slices). The app owns no table, action or event.
## Reuse sources

The served action registry, the read models of S05–S20, the approval primitive, the signed parity contract and the OIDC helper. Each is named in the requirements and data catalogs; the app reuses them rather than forking a read or write path.
## Inception units

The S12 slice plan with its screen table and gate. No separate inception directory exists for S12, so the project brief and inception analysis are authored from the plan's sections and the record, and this output is the brief the close gate reads.
## Dependencies

S12 needs S01, S02, S04, S05–S11, S17 and S18; every one is built. The cutover is S14's and reuses the suite. No dependency is open construction, and the gate work depends on no other unit.
## Acceptance

The plan's gate: every spec asserts empty, error and happy, and the coverage table has no orphan. The coverage half is met; the state half is carried by a test-only unit, and the closure review is written only after it lands.
## Capabilities

The web app capability covers boards and work, authoring, operations and measurement, with one app and one cutover. No other capability may fork the screen set or the action client.
## Plan

`docs/plans/slices/S12-ui-buildout.md` with its 22-row screen table, its build order and its gate. The tranche plan places S12 in tranche 10 with T5; the authorisation is the tranche review's act.

# Evidence

## Claim

S12 delivers the web app over the served actions, with the coverage half of its gate met and its state half measured and carried by a test-only unit.
## Evidence

46 screen modules under `apps/web/src/screens`; 51 Playwright specs, 21 for the declared screens; the action client in `apps/web/src/api.rs`; the signed parity contract (1300 rows; used 218, rare 295, unused 543, dropped 244) with its native map present; the real-binary harness in `apps/web/playwright.config.ts`.
## Verification

`python3 scripts/check-parity.py --require-native` reports the signed contract and its native map; the suite runs with `npx playwright test` against the real binary and a seeded database. The spec audit in #965 is the instrument for the gate's state half, and the compile verdict is the repository's preflight.
## Links

`docs/plans/slices/S12-ui-buildout.md`, `acceptance/programme/S12.toml`, the parity contract under `parity/`, and the screen modules and specs the catalog names.
## Gap

The gate's state half is partial: three happy-path-only specs, six missing an empty state, two missing a rendered refusal and no dedicated eval-run spec. #965 carries the repair; the closure review and the declared closure outputs wait for it. No other gap is claimed.
